['Soon I will tie up the field valley and go to meet my love in the field valley.  
I’m about to finish tying up the whole field valley, but I lose my golden broom and leave.  
The wind softly blows, the clouds gently drift, and even the neighbor’s daughter seems gentle in my eyes.  
The wind blows and becomes the southeast wind, and tears flow and become the Daedong River.  
()  
Oh, you young men in your prime, upon seeing white hair, do not oppose me.  
While white hair on a man might be useful, white hair on a person has no use.  
A pumpkin might still taste good when old, but an old person has no use.  
If we live like this and grow old, when would a friend come to visit me? ()  
I want to go, I too want to go, as long as life is good I want to go.  
This way or that way, I will die eventually; when I die, will a friend come to visit me?  

Yellow, yellow, a new spring breeze gently caresses, softly stirring the village.  
What is that bachelor talking about? You need to perform a ritual for the village to stir.  
Would a chicken cause the village to stir?  

I want to finish tying all the fields, but the owner loses his temper and leaves.  

Across the mountain, I carried a big child on my back and, seeing a bachelor, stepped sideways.  
Why did you step sideways when looking at him? Because of the southeast wind blowing sideways.  

The maiden from Gurye valley has not yet married, so she grabs a dart frog and sheds tears.  
If the mountain is high, the valley is deep; can a little woman’s heart be shallow?  

Yellow, yellow, a new spring breeze softly washes through every alley.  
This rice field cicada hides among the rice plants, quietly shimmering like a beautiful thread of fate.', "- Planting rice seedlings in this paddy field, even if the leaves wither, it is not a problem.

don’t boast about being the prettiest beauty in the city.  
The sun setting in the west,  
who can stop it?  
The water flowing in the East Sea,  
when will it return again?  
Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, King Wen and Duke Zhou,  
the great sages all have passed on,  
morality has declined,  
all ancient sages lost,  
but none escaped death once.

is noted in the Five Classics.

General Xiao Zhi, renowned for words,

The spring breeze and the moon call and sing,  
but only sorrowful cries remain.  
The eternal hero, the failed king,  
built a high palace,  
wished for immortality,  
built the Great Wall for a thousand miles,  
received orders from the six kingdoms,  
the three thousand palace maids wore mourning clothes,  
the five hundred girls and boys  
were sent to search for the herb of immortality on the Three Divine Mountains,  
but they could not find it,  
there has been no news until yesterday.  
Hello, military camp folks,  
the sun is setting today,  
shall we sing one song through the night?  
Listening to the old man’s words,  
even the shaman's rituals are feeble,  
and the rainstorm lasts only three stones (a short time),  
should we withdraw for a while?  
Over there, in the bean field,  
last year we planted beans,  
what will we plant this year?  
Shall we plow the field with a cow,  
and try planting five grains?  
We planted five grains,  
received sunlight by day,  
and dew by night,  
ears sprouted in Baekno field,  
the entire field is ripening.  
In the ripening grain field,  
birds, birds are flying in,  
all kinds of wild birds fly in.  
If I try to name all their names,  
the day is too short.  
Among them, the most fearsome bird,  
with two long legs,  
and a blunt beak—  
I alone cannot drive it away,  
everyone here,  
drive away all wild birds.  
They are flying in from all sides,  
neighbors gathered here,

woo-eo-woo-i,  
wi-i."]

['Three years after getting married, my mother-in-law said,
"Go spit out the baby," and when I went out to the field,
Why were the ridges in the field as long as a mountain?
After tending one ridge and the space between ridges, all the shoots came out,
Even after tending two ridges, the field looked like a mountain,
Even after tending two ridges, others' lunches appeared, but mine did not.
I was so hungry I thought I’d die, so I went home,
But my sister-in-law, like a poisonous snake, came inside without tending the field.
I came in because I was hungry.
No matter what, I can’t live in this in-law’s house.
After three years, they gave me old soybean paste on a plate,
And sticky barley rice in a bowl.
Eating this, no matter how much I think, I can’t live—I can’t live in this house.
When I came to marry, I tore one piece of clothing to make a bundle,
Tore two more pieces for my bag,
Tore one more for my headscarf,
And tore twelve pieces to make a quilt and a bag, and then I shaved my head.
I went back to my parents' village and visited my parents first.
"Why did you come back so soon?"
When I said I was going home, they said, "The dog is barking. It’s barking."
I gave you everything, yet you don’t even recognize me.
I came to see you, the one I gave rice to.
My mother said, “Dear, why can’t you live in that house?
How did you end up like this?”
I packed my sacks with bundles and scarves and went back,
My mother’s eyes darkened, saying, “Oh, why can’t you live in that house?”
No matter how much I think, I can’t live there.
Maybe it’s because I chose the wrong husband, where is that husband now?
How could he be so cruel? “That’s just how it is.”
Mother-in-law, after leaving that proud one behind, you took me in?
“When a daughter-in-law is like that, that’s what the mother-in-law says.”
If you left that proud one and took me in, you shouldn’t have troubled me so much.
You cooked and cooked, why did you trouble me so?
No matter how much I think, I can’t live.
“That’s how it went. It’s a hardship.”', 'Three days after getting married, I was told to go weed the millet field.  
Going to weed the millet field, I found the field was as hard as stone,  
The field I was to weed was as hard as rice husks.  
I weeded one row, then two rows,  
After three or four hours of helping,  
Even though lunch was served,  
Our lunch was not brought out.  
When I went back inside the house,  
The love door (room to the in-laws) was slammed open,  
And my father-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three or four rows again."  
"Hey, woman, go away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
The door to the main room was slammed open,  
And my mother-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three rows repeatedly."  
"Hey, woman, shoo away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
I went into my room,  
Spread out nine panels of eaves,  
Made a hat with one panel,  
A scarf with two panels,  
A basket with four panels,  
And then I went to visit my parental home.  
Turning one corner,  
The district chief was standing there,  
"District chief, district chief, please shave my head,"  
After shaving one corner,  
Tears welled up in my eyes,  
After shaving two corners,  
Tears streamed down,  
After shaving front and back hair,  
I cried and cried.  
On that path, I arrived at my parental home,  
"Please lend me some millet,"  
Falling on the millet floor, I spilled all over the ground.  
My mother said,  
"Use the broom to sweep it away,"  
"Break the millet stalks and eat them,"  
But I am not the kind of person who eats from the tip of a broom or a millet stalk.  
"Let's eat dinner till sunset,"  
My mother said,  
"The Bodhisattva will bless us with offerings and dinner,"  
"There are cows in the stable and dogs under the floor,"  
I fell asleep in the feedroom,  
The moon was bright and the stars were bright.  
My mother said,  
"Seeing the bright moon and stars,  
You should be able to see the piece of phoenix wood,

Looking around the feedroom,  
"Child, you came?"  
They cried sadly.  
After explaining everything,  
Compassion arose naturally,  
I lived there for three or four years,  
And then went to my married home.  
At my mother-in-law's grave, chrysanthemums bloomed,  
At my father-in-law's grave, forsythias bloomed,  
At my husband's grave, hibiscus flowers waved gently in the wind.

- Folklore lyrics', 'Three days after getting married, what my mother-in-law said:

Where have you been, my daughter-in-law? Where have you been, my daughter-in-law?  
Do you want to weed the field or the rice paddy? The field need not be weeded,  
but how can the rice paddy be weeded? She said, "Follow the dog."  
So I followed the dog and found it had gone to the field.  
Weeding one row, then two rows,  
my finger that once wore a silver ring,  
why now is it tied with hemp string?  
The silk apron I once wore,  
why now is it a cotton apron?  
The floral shoes I used to wear,  
why now are they woven from straw?  
When I looked around carefully,  
as evening came,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

When I went inside the house,  
the front and middle doors were all locked.  
"Sister-in-law, open the door!  
I’ve been weeding the fields," I said.  
In the scorching sun of a cold day,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
This is what my father-in-law said.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
My mother-in-law said sharply:  
"Go rot away in your own house!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you waiting for the right day and time?"  

Crossing the southern hill with determination,  
she dipped the rice she ate the night before  
into a bowl of soup,  
and wiped the crumbs of three years’ worth of meals  
onto a small dish.  
Feeling sorry and downhearted,  
she ate those all up,  
then entered my room.  

She took nine pieces of the widow’s dress—  
carefully unfolded each layer—  
one piece was torn,  
one piece was shaped into a cone,  
one piece was finely cut,  
and when one roll was spun round and round,  
my husband who had gone to Seoul came down  
wearing a hat like the heavens,  
riding a horse above the attic,  
and dismounting with a bang.  

Startled, I said:  
“Hold my wrists tightly,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Where are you going? Where are you going?  
I can’t live anymore,  
I can’t live in your house.  
Your parents are frightening,  
your younger siblings are frightening.  
Their parents always demand 'buy me',  
and your siblings also keep demanding 'buy me'.  
Come with me, come with me!  
I just can’t live here, I just can’t live here!”  

When one turn of the roll went by,  
a friend came out and called,  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
cut my hair, please.”  
After she cut one side of my hair,  
the dew started to fall naturally,  
after shaving the double braids,  
a great wailing naturally arose.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my maternal home.”  

Entering the gate of my parental home,  
“Please give me alms, please give me alms.”  
My eldest son-in-law cursed,  
“Among these people, some look like our sister-in-law.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
“Should I give you glutinous rice liquor or non-glutinous rice liquor?  
I throw away the glutinous and non-glutinous rice,  
please give me millet.”  
I gather millet endlessly in a bottomless pit until sunset.  

My sibling, going to the village school,  
said, “Among these people, some resemble our elder sister.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
My mother is ill,  
and some resemble my daughter.  
"I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike."  

As the day ended,  
I thought I’d stay a while in this house,  
but there was no room, so I couldn’t sleep.  
Trying to sleep under the floor,  
I sat there but couldn’t sleep because worries came flooding.  
It was almost midnight.  

“Mother, mother, my mother,  
I didn't realize this was how it would be.”  
I repeatedly knocked on the three doors,  
when my mother opened the door,  
she cursed loudly,  
and clasping both hands together,  
she wailed loudly.  

As day broke,  
I went around with my friend,  
traveling north, south, east, and west.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my marital home.”  

When I went begging at my marital home,  
at my father-in-law’s grave, the dragon’s spirit flower bloomed,  
at my mother-in-law’s grave, the wild grass flower bloomed,  
and at my husband’s grave, the hibiscus flower bloomed.  

Looking around my house,  
the hemp field had become untended.  
“Let me split it, let me split it,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Let me split just half,  
let’s try living in the afterlife.”  
When splitting half,  
he entered that grave.']
